eyebrow: Statistics & Probability for Data Science · Chapter 4, Lesson 19
subtitle: No formula for your statistic? Resample your own data instead.

steps.label: DRAW n FROM YOUR OWN n
steps.sub: Some values repeat, some are left out

code:
orders = rng.lognormal(3.5, 0.8, size=40).round(2)   # mean 35.32, median 25.4
boot_means = np.array([rng.choice(orders, 40, replace=True).mean() for _ in range(B)])
print(round(boot_means.std(ddof=1), 2), round(stats.sem(orders), 2))
# 4.42  4.50  -- bootstrap SE matches the formula closely
caption: The bootstrap's standard error, computed with zero formulas -- just resampling.

eyebrow: The percentile interval vs. the t-interval
code:
lo, hi = np.percentile(boot_means, [2.5, 97.5])
print(lo, hi)   # 27.5  44.76

# t-interval on the same data: 26.22 to 44.42 (forced symmetric)
caption: The bootstrap interval shifts right, reflecting the real skew -- the t-interval can't do that.

eyebrow: Bootstrapping a median -- no formula exists
code:
idx = rng.integers(0, len(orders), size=(B, len(orders)))
boot_medians = np.median(orders[idx], axis=1)   # vectorized -- fast
lo, hi = np.percentile(boot_medians, [2.5, 97.5])
print(lo, hi)   # 19.98  42.59
caption: Wide, honestly: 40 observations say little about the middle of a skewed distribution.

code:
res = stats.bootstrap((orders,), np.median, n_resamples=9999,
                      method="percentile", random_state=1)
res.confidence_interval   # low 19.98, high 42.59

res2 = stats.bootstrap((orders,), np.mean, n_resamples=9999)
# default method "BCa" corrects for bias/skew
caption: BCa's mean interval (28.76-47.59) shifts further right than the plain percentile version.

eyebrow: Where it shines: comparing two groups
code:
ia = rng.integers(0, 60, size=(B, 60)); ib = rng.integers(0, 60, size=(B, 60))
diffs = b[ib].mean(axis=1) - a[ia].mean(axis=1)
print(b.mean()-a.mean(), np.percentile(diffs, [2.5, 97.5]))
# 1.93  [-12.12, 15.78]
caption: Interval comfortably includes zero -- the data can't distinguish these groups. A preview of Ch. 5.
